reasoning: The scene reads as a long valley/corridor with a broad open center, dense tree masses framing both sides, and a few exposed rock/terrain features breaking up the floor. Good lighting anchors should spread across the valley: one on the left-side opening near the water/rocks, one centered in the main clearing, one on the right-side slope by the exposed stone, and one farther back where the valley narrows. I’m keeping anchors spaced apart and based on distinct geometric opportunities: open ground, edge-of-wall/tree line, and isolated rock clusters.

anchors.traits: Large surrounding terrain mass with a broad open floor area nearby; good place for a light to sit over open ground without immediately intersecting dense geometry.
Central scene hub relative to the whole layout; the widest open clearing is around it, making it suitable for a general fill light placed above the main open span.
Right-side edge zone with rocky wall-like forms and a narrower pocket of space; suitable for a side-positioned light near the cliff line.
Left-mid valley margin with water/rock shapes and some open air above the slope; a light can sit just off the denser foliage line here.
Farther-back narrowing section of the valley where the tree lines converge; open vertical space but constrained horizontal clearance, good for a distant accent placed high enough to avoid the canopy.
